faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about building PCs

q1.question: What is the minimum budget for a gaming PC?
q1.answer: The minimum budget depends on your goals. For 1080p gaming at 60 FPS in modern AAA games, consider around $600-800. For competitive games (CS2, Valorant) you can start with $500. For 1440p or 4K, the budget increases significantly to $1200 or more.

q2.question: Do I need a dedicated graphics card for gaming?
q2.answer: Yes, for most modern games, a dedicated GPU is essential. While modern CPUs have integrated graphics that can run light and older games, AAA games and modern competitive titles require a dedicated graphics card for good performance.

q3.question: How much RAM do I need?
q3.answer: For gaming: 16GB is the current recommended standard. For professional work or content creation: 32GB is ideal, especially for video editing or 3D modeling. For basic use: 8GB may suffice, but 16GB offers better longevity.

q4.question: What's the difference between 1080p, 1440p, and 4K?
q4.answer: 1080p (Full HD): 1920x1080 pixels, easier to run, ideal for smaller budgets. 1440p (2K): 2560x1440 pixels, excellent balance between visual quality and performance. 4K (Ultra HD): 3840x2160 pixels, best visual quality, but requires much more powerful and expensive hardware.

q5.question: What is FPS and why is it important?
q5.answer: FPS (Frames Per Second) is the number of images displayed per second. 60 FPS: Smooth experience for most games. 120-144 FPS: Ideal for competitive gaming, offers advantage in reaction and precision. 240+ FPS: For professional and elite competitive players. Higher FPS reduces input lag and makes movement smoother.

q6.question: Should I choose Intel or AMD for the processor?
q6.answer: Both are excellent choices. AMD Ryzen: Generally better value for money, excellent for multitasking and content creation. Intel Core: Traditionally better performance in pure gaming, especially in top models. The choice depends on your specific budget and use case. We recommend comparing specific models in your price range.

q7.question: What is RGB lighting and do I need it?
q7.answer: RGB is customizable colored lighting on PC components. Doesn't affect performance, it's purely aesthetic. Pros: Attractive visual, customization. Cons: Additional cost, can distract. If budget is tight, prioritize performance over aesthetics. If you have room in your budget and value appearance, RGB can enhance the experience.

q8.question: How can I upgrade my PC in the future?
q8.answer: Common upgrades by impact order: 1. GPU: Biggest impact on gaming performance. 2. Add RAM: If you have less than 16GB. 3. SSD: If still using HDD, drastically improves speed. 4. CPU: Usually last priority, unless it's a bottleneck. Make sure the power supply and motherboard support future upgrades.

q9.question: Do I need liquid cooling?
q9.answer: Not necessarily. Air cooling: Cheaper, reliable, sufficient for most users. Liquid cooling (AIO): Better for extreme overclocking or aesthetics. Custom loop: Only for enthusiasts. For most PCs, a good air cooler is sufficient and more economical.

q10.question: What size power supply do I need?
q10.answer: Depends on your components. Basic/office PC: 400-500W. Mid-range gaming PC: 600-750W. High-end gaming PC: 750-850W. Extreme PC/workstation: 850W+. Always use a quality PSU (80+ Bronze minimum) with 100-200W headroom above estimated consumption for efficiency and longevity.
